title: Family, adjectives and possessives
summary: Talk about your family: possessives agree with the noun (ma sœur, mon frère), adjectives agree and mostly follow it.
focus: Family words, possessive adjectives, and adjective agreement and position
content:
## Possessives: mon, ma, mes

A possessive agrees with the **thing owned**, not with the owner:

| | masculine | feminine | plural |
|---|---|---|---|
| my | **mon** père | **ma** mère | **mes** parents |
| your (tu) | **ton** frère | **ta** sœur | **tes** cousins |
| his / her | **son** fils | **sa** fille | **ses** enfants |
| our | **notre** oncle | **notre** tante | **nos** grands-parents |
| your (vous) | **votre** mari | **votre** femme | **vos** cousines |
| their | **leur** père | **leur** mère | **leurs** enfants |

So **sa mère** is *his mother* or *her mother*. The context tells you whose. Before a vowel or silent **h**, use **mon / ton / son** even for a feminine noun: **mon amie**, **ton école**, **son histoire**.

## Adjectives agree

An adjective takes the gender and number of its noun. Add **-e** for feminine, **-s** for plural, **-es** for both:

| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| masculine | grand | grands |
| feminine | grande | grandes |

An adjective that already ends in **-e** does not change for the feminine: **un frère jeune**, **une sœur jeune**. A few change more:

- **beau**, feminine **belle** (beautiful, handsome), plural **beaux / belles**
- **vieux**, feminine **vieille** (old), plural **vieux / vieilles**
- **gentil**, feminine **gentille** (kind), plural **gentils / gentilles**
- **bon**, feminine **bonne** (good)

The final consonant you don't hear in **grand** is heard in **grande**. That is often how you hear the feminine.

## Before or after the noun

Most adjectives come **after** the noun, unlike in English: **une voiture rouge**, **un frère intelligent**, **une tante sympa**.

A short list of very common adjectives comes **before** it: **petit**, **grand**, **beau**, **jeune**, **vieux**, **bon**.

- **une petite maison** (a small house)
- **un grand jardin** (a big garden)
- **une belle ville** (a beautiful town)
- **un bon restaurant** (a good restaurant)

Both kinds can share one noun, one before and one after: **une petite voiture rouge** (a small red car).

quiz.explanation: Mère is feminine singular and starts with a consonant, so 'my' is ma: ma mère.
Amie is feminine, but it starts with a vowel, so ma becomes mon: mon amie.
hints: Look at the first letter of amie.

quiz.explanation: Grands-parents is plural, so 'my' is mes: mes grands-parents.
Sa agrees with sœur (feminine), not with the owner. Sa sœur means his sister or her sister.
hints: Possessives agree with the thing owned.

quiz.explanation: Sœur is feminine singular, so add -e: ma sœur est grande.

quiz.prompt: Choose the correct phrase: 'a beautiful house'.
quiz.explanation: Beau is one of the adjectives that go before the noun, and its feminine is belle: une belle maison.
hints: Beau is on the short list that goes first.

quiz.prompt: La maison de ma tante est ___. (vieux)
quiz.explanation: Maison is feminine, and the feminine of vieux is vieille.
Cousins is masculine plural, so gentil takes -s: mes cousins sont gentils.
Colours come after the noun: une voiture rouge. Only a short list (petit, grand, beau, jeune, vieux, bon) goes before.
hints: Is rouge on the short list?

listening.text: Mon frère est petit.
listening.meaning: My brother is short.

listening.text: Nos grands-parents habitent à Lille.
listening.meaning: Our grandparents live in Lille.
listening.note: Nos is the plural of notre.

listening.text: Ma tante a une belle maison.
listening.meaning: My aunt has a beautiful house.
listening.note: Belle is the feminine of beau, and it goes before the noun.

listening.text: Mon amie Claire a un vieux chat.
listening.meaning: My friend Claire has an old cat.
listening.note: New word: le chat = the cat.

listening.text: Sa fille est grande et très gentille.
listening.meaning: Her daughter is tall and very kind.

listening.text: Leur fils travaille dans une petite boulangerie.
listening.meaning: Their son works in a small bakery.
listening.note: New word: la boulangerie = the bakery.

listening.text: Mes cousines sont jeunes et elles habitent à Paris.
listening.meaning: My cousins are young and they live in Paris.
listening.note: Jeune already ends in -e: only the plural -s is added.

listening.text: Votre mari est un homme très intelligent et très drôle.
listening.meaning: Your husband is a very intelligent and very funny man.

guide.tip: Hear the feminine: grand ends silent, grande ends on a d. Petit / petite, gentil / gentille work the same way.

concept.title: Bel and vieil
concept.markdown:
Before a masculine noun that starts with a vowel, **beau** becomes **bel** and **vieux** becomes **vieil**, so the words flow:

- **un bel homme** (a handsome man)
- **un vieil ami** (an old friend)

conversations.title: Family photos
conversations.scenario: Lucie shows her friend Malik photos of her family on her phone.

bites.title: Agree with the thing owned
bites.rule: Mon / ma / mes follow the noun, not the owner: ma mère, mon père, mes parents. Sa mère means his or her mother.

bites.title: Mon before a vowel
bites.rule: Before a vowel or a silent h, ma / ta / sa become mon / ton / son, even for a feminine noun.

bites.title: -e, -s, -es
bites.rule: Adjectives agree: grand, grande, grands, grandes. Watch beau / belle, vieux / vieille, gentil / gentille.

bites.title: Most go after
bites.rule: Most adjectives follow the noun (une voiture rouge). Petit, grand, beau, jeune, vieux, bon go before it.

sorts.title: Mon, ma or mes?
sorts.why: Use mon with a masculine noun or before a vowel, ma with a feminine noun and mes with a plural.

sorts.title: Before or after the noun?
sorts.why: Petit, grand, beau, jeune, vieux and bon go before; most others, colours and nationalities included, go after.

spots.why: Before a vowel, ma becomes mon: mon amie.
The feminine of beau is belle.
Mère is feminine; the owner doesn't matter: sa mère.

builds.text: Mon oncle a une vieille voiture.
builds.meaning: My uncle has an old car.

realm.content:
## La famille à Eldmark

In Eldmark, families are legendary. Borin **et son vieux père** forge **une belle épée** at Deepanvil; la mage Séla **et sa sœur** live in **une petite tour**. Possessives follow the noun, adjectives agree: **un guerrier fort, une guerrière forte, des nains forts**.

vocabulary.example: Borin et son père travaillent à Deepanvil.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Borin and his father work in Deepanvil.

vocabulary.example: Séla et sa sœur sont mages.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Séla and her sister are mages.

vocabulary.example: Le frère de Nym est chasseur.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nym's brother is a hunter.

vocabulary.example: Leur fille est une grande guerrière.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Their daughter is a great warrior.

vocabulary.example: Le paladin a une belle épée.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The paladin has a beautiful sword.

vocabulary.example: La vieille prêtresse habite dans la tour.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The old priestess lives in the tower.

vocabulary.example: Mon oncle est un nain très fort.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My uncle is a very strong dwarf.

vocabulary.example: Mon épée est vieille.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My sword is old.

vocabulary.example: La tour est grande.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The tower is tall.

vocabulary.example: La guerrière est forte.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The warrior is strong.

bites.title: Famille de héros
bites.rule: Son épée, sa tour, ses frères: the possessive follows the noun. Adjectives agree too: un nain fort, une naine forte.
bites.example: Séla et sa sœur habitent dans une petite tour.
bites.example_meaning: Séla and her sister live in a small tower.

spots.why: Père is masculine: son père, whoever the owner is.

sorts.title: Son, sa or ses in Eldmark?
sorts.why: Use son with a masculine noun or before a vowel (son épée), sa with a feminine noun and ses with a plural.

quiz.explanation: Épée is feminine, but it starts with a vowel, so sa becomes son: son épée.
hints: Look at the first letter of épée.

quiz.explanation: Guerrière is feminine singular: add -e, forte.

meadowbrook.content:
## La famille à Meadowbrook

Nora's family farm is small but busy. Here **sa grand-mère** waters **les belles fraises**, **son petit frère** feeds **le vieux mouton**, and **leurs poules** are **noires**. Possessives follow the noun, adjectives agree: **un petit mouton, une petite poule, des poules noires**.

vocabulary.example: Mon petit frère aime les poules.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My little brother likes the hens.

vocabulary.example: Mes grands-parents ont une vieille ferme.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandparents have an old farm.

vocabulary.example: Ma tante est la mairesse de Meadowbrook.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My aunt is the mayor of Meadowbrook.

vocabulary.example: Ma cousine aide Rosa à la graineterie.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My cousin helps Rosa at the seed shop.

vocabulary.example: Les fraises sont belles cette année.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The strawberries are beautiful this year.

vocabulary.example: Notre vache est vieille mais gentille.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Our cow is old but gentle.

vocabulary.example: Le mouton de Nora est vieux.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora's sheep is old.

vocabulary.example: Nos poules sont noires.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Our hens are black.

vocabulary.example: La vache noire est à mon oncle.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The black cow belongs to my uncle.

bites.title: Ma ferme, mes animaux
bites.rule: Mon mouton, ma poule, mes vaches: the possessive follows the animal. Adjectives agree: un petit mouton, une petite poule.

listening.text: Le vieux mouton mange.
listening.meaning: The old sheep is eating.
listening.note: New word: le mouton = the sheep.

listening.text: Ma poule noire est très vieille.
listening.meaning: My black hen is very old.
listening.note: New word: la poule = the hen.

listening.text: Ma grand-mère arrose les belles fraises.
listening.meaning: My grandmother waters the beautiful strawberries.

listening.text: Leur ferme est petite mais jolie.
listening.meaning: Their farm is small but pretty.

listening.text: Mon frère et ma cousine pêchent ensemble.
listening.meaning: My brother and my cousin fish together.

builds.text: Ma tante a une vieille vache.
builds.meaning: My aunt has an old cow.

spots.why: Ses deux is plural, so the noun is plural too: ses deux moutons.

sorts.title: Masculine or feminine on the farm?
sorts.why: The adjective agrees with the noun's gender: un petit mouton, une petite vache.

quiz.explanation: Poules is plural, so 'our' is nos: nos poules.
Vache is feminine, and the feminine of vieux is vieille.

rustwake.content:
## La famille à Rustwake

In the scrap village, families stick together. Léo **et sa sœur** fix **un vieux robot**, Marta **et son mari** repair **des radios**. Possessives follow the noun, adjectives agree: **une combinaison bleue, des combinaisons bleues**.

vocabulary.example: Léo et sa sœur réparent la radio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Léo and his sister repair the radio.

vocabulary.example: Le mari de Marta est fouilleur.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta's husband is a scavenger.

vocabulary.example: Mon père habite encore dans le Dôme.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My father still lives in the Dome.

vocabulary.example: Nos grands-parents racontent la vie avant le désert.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Our grandparents tell of life before the desert.

vocabulary.example: Le vieux robot jardinier est gentil.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The old gardener robot is kind.

vocabulary.example: Marta a une belle radio-montre.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta has a beautiful wrist radio.

vocabulary.example: Notre robot est petit.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Our robot is small.

vocabulary.example: Ma combinaison est bleue.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My jumpsuit is blue.

vocabulary.example: Leurs combinaisons sont bleues.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Their jumpsuits are blue.

bites.title: Famille du désert
bites.rule: Son robot, sa combinaison, ses écrous: the possessive follows the noun. Adjectives agree: un robot bleu, une combinaison bleue.
bites.example: Léo et sa sœur réparent un vieux robot.
bites.example_meaning: Léo and his sister repair an old robot.

listening.text: Ta combinaison est vieille et bleue.
listening.meaning: Your jumpsuit is old and blue.
listening.note: New word: la combinaison = the jumpsuit.

listening.text: Notre robot est vieux.
listening.meaning: Our robot is old.
listening.note: New word: le robot = the robot.

listening.text: Léo et sa sœur cherchent des écrous.
listening.meaning: Léo and his sister are looking for nuts.

listening.text: Leur fils est un petit fouilleur.
listening.meaning: Their son is a little scavenger.

listening.text: Mon oncle a une vieille radio-montre.
listening.meaning: My uncle has an old wrist radio.

builds.text: Léo et sa sœur réparent la radio.
builds.meaning: Léo and his sister repair the radio.

spots.sentence: Marta et sa mari réparent des radios.

sorts.title: Bleu, bleue, bleus or bleues?
sorts.why: The adjective agrees: -e for feminine, -s for plural, -es for both.

quiz.explanation: Combinaisons is feminine plural, so add -es: bleues.
Son agrees with robot (masculine), not with the owner: son robot is his robot or her robot.
hints: Possessives agree with the thing owned.
